VSPH / BRAND GUIDELINES02 / OUR IDENTITY
02 / OUR IDENTITY

A recognizable expression of progress.

Primary logo

The horizontal signature pairs the angular V symbol with the VSPH wordmark. Use this arrangement as the default brand identifier.

Standalone symbol

Use the V symbol in compact spaces where the VSPH name is already clear, such as an avatar or an application launcher.

Keep the mark and wordmark in their original relationship. Treat the complete lockup as one piece of artwork.

01 / PRIMARY HORIZONTAL SIGNATURE
The visual idea

Structure meets possibility.

The V creates a clear foundation. Ascending pixels suggest digital progress and forward movement.

The logo shown throughout this guide is a reference reconstruction. Original geometry, spacing and color gradients must be verified against VSPH’s master artwork before release.

Choose the right version.

Clarity begins with the background.

Select the version that preserves the complete silhouette and keeps the VSPH name immediately readable.

Use solid, quiet backgrounds. On photographs, place the logo in a clean area or on a solid brand-color panel.

Production rule
For embroidery, engraving and one-ink print, use a verified monochrome master. Never simulate a color logo with an untested conversion.

Primary / light background

Default for documents and white interfaces.

Reversed / navy background

For covers and darker brand environments.

Monochrome / black

For single-color reproduction.

Monochrome / navy

For light-blue fields and restricted production.

VSPH / BRAND GUIDELINES03 / VISUAL LANGUAGE
03 / VISUAL LANGUAGE

Color should clarify, not compete.

Start with restraint.

Use white and grey for most content, navy for hierarchy, core blue for actions, and light blue for selective accents.

60% NEUTRALS / 25% NAVY
10% CORE BLUE / 5% LIGHT BLUE

A starting balance for content layouts. Covers and section pages may use a dominant navy or blue field.

Text contrast

Target at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for qualifying large text. Test the actual foreground and background together.

VSPH / BRAND GUIDELINES03 / VISUAL LANGUAGE
03 / VISUAL LANGUAGE

A hierarchy that does the work.

Digital type scale

The supplied scale uses generous leading and deliberate weight changes. Set one clear entry point, then guide the reader through the content.

Keep paragraphs left-aligned. Aim for 45–75 characters per line. Use sentence case for ordinary headings.

Responsive & print use

On small screens, reduce H1 to 36/44 px and keep body text at 16/24 px or larger.

For A4 documents, start with 28–36 pt headings and 10.5–12 pt body copy. Check the printed reading size.

VSPH / BRAND GUIDELINES03 / VISUAL LANGUAGE
03 / VISUAL LANGUAGE

Structure creates confidence.

Use a disciplined grid.

Align headings, images and captions to shared edges. Build one strong focal point and allow generous open space around it.

For desktop layouts, use a 12-column grid. For mobile, use four columns and 20–24 px side margins.

Document starting point
Landscape A4. Approximately 15 mm outer margins. Use a 1:2 guidance-to-demonstration split where a rule needs a visual example.

A visual language of forward motion.

Progress lines

A proposed supporting graphic system: fine angular paths and a small rhythm of ascending square details, inspired by the V symbol.

Use the device to frame a story, connect content or suggest momentum. Keep the logo visually distinct.

Working rules
Use a single direction of movement. Keep strokes light. Limit detail to one area. Keep text on a quiet field.

Never turn the motif into a replacement logo or scatter pixels around body copy.

with purpose.

A SUPPORTING DEVICE / NOT A SECOND LOGO

Light application
Blue application

Use line work as decoration. Never rely on it to carry essential information.

People doing meaningful work

Choose candid collaboration, attentive interaction and believable business environments. Keep skin tones natural.

04 / VOICE & MESSAGING

Say what matters, in the right order.

Lead with the audience’s need.

Use the core message to establish the brand, then add the most relevant capability and business context.

Support value statements with clear explanations. Use evidence when it exists; never invent results to strengthen a story.

Elevator introduction

VSPH builds scalable web, mobile and enterprise applications. We work with businesses to turn ideas into practical digital solutions that support how they operate and grow.

Core message

Building What’s Next.

Enterprise Software Solutions for a Smarter Tomorrow.

VALUE STATEMENT

Explain the value

Building scalable digital solutions. Helping businesses innovate, streamline and grow.

CAPABILITY MESSAGE

Make it relevant

Connect web, mobile, custom software or consulting to the reader’s specific need.

Close with a useful action

Discuss your project. Explore our services.

NAME & TERMINOLOGY

Use the name consistently

Write VSPH in capitals. Keep product or service labels clear and descriptive.

STYLE & CLARITY

Write with intention

Prefer active verbs, short sentences and sentence case. Explain unfamiliar abbreviations on first use.

EVIDENCE & ACCURACY

Make claims responsibly

Use client names, certifications and performance results only when verified and approved.

Tone can adapt to context: more concise in interfaces, more explanatory in proposals, and warmer in project communication. The underlying voice stays consistent.

A digital presence with purpose.

Website & interface

Use navy to establish the brand, a clear message to orient visitors, and core blue to identify the primary action.

Keep navigation simple. Group services around user needs. Give each section one clear next step.

Digital house rules
Use visible keyboard focus. Pair errors with helpful text. Prefer 44 × 44 px interaction targets. Provide meaningful image alternatives.

The target size is a proposed VSPH house standard. Test complete pages against WCAG 2.2 AA before release.

This is a production checklist, not a claim that original source assets were supplied. The reconstructed logo and new standards in this edition require brand-owner verification.

Suggested file naming

VSPH_Logo_Primary_RGB_v1.svg
VSPH_BrandGuidelines_v1.0.pdf

Export & quality controls

Digital delivery

Use SVG for scalable marks and icons. Use transparent PNG where vectors are unsupported. Export in sRGB and inspect at the target viewing size.

Print delivery

Keep artwork vector where possible. For raster images, target 300 ppi at final size. Agree bleed, color profile and PDF settings with the printer; approve a physical proof.

Accessible documents

Keep text selectable. Verify reading order, document language, meaningful links and image alternatives in the final PDF workflow.

This PDF is optimized for screen review. A printer-specific press file and formal accessibility validation are separate production checks.

Make every detail feel like VSPH.

A shared responsibility

Assign a brand steward to maintain approved artwork, templates and guideline versions. Keep current files together and archive superseded editions.

Review new, high-visibility applications before release. Record the reason and date for any change to the system.

Before you publish

The checklist applies to each final deliverable. Complete verification of reconstructed artwork before adopting the master asset library.

Clear space and readable minimum size
Exact brand colors and suitable contrast
Consistent Inter typography and hierarchy
Clear, useful and accurate language
Verified claims and company details
Appropriate imagery and usage rights
